Researching Efficacy of the Official Air Force Qualifying Test and Test of Basic Aviation Skills Test-Familiarization Software 

Subject: Research Participation Opportunity

You are invited to participate in research into your experiences using the Official AFOQT & TBAS Test-Familiarization Software BETA (OATTS-BETA) in readying to take the Air Force Officer Qualifying Test (AFOQT) and the Test of Basic Aviation Skills (TBAS). Your responses and user data will be anonymous and will only be used to understand and potentially improve the experience and efficacy of OATTS. This work is sponsored by the Air Force Research Laboratory and Air Education Training Command. Please take time to read this message in its entirety before deciding whether to take part in this research and use this experimental software.

At the completion of your focused modules, you will be prompted to export your OATTS-BETA data and submit it via email for researchers to collate. This data will include how many times you completed each module, answers to pre- and post-tests with knowledge and reaction questions. 

By exporting and sharing your data via email, you are affirming your understanding of this informed consent and agreeing to participate in the research. 
Key information you should know:

•	The purpose of the study is to understand reactions to and the efficacy of using the OATTS tool. 
•	We estimate completion will vary widely, depending on how many and which modules are completed.
•	Risks or discomforts from participating in this study are typical of what is experienced in an office setting (e.g., eye strain).
•	Taking part in this study is voluntary. You can discontinue participation at any time without penalty or loss. 
•	We will take the following precautions to maintain the confidentiality of your data: we will not link any identifiers to your responses. Electronic data will be password-protected/encrypted. After data is collected, it will be examined for any Personal Identifying Information, which will be deleted immediately. The data will only be accessible to the research team that is conducting the study. No person in your direct chain of command will be able to know if you have participated and will never have access to your responses. Data will be deleted at the conclusion of this work.  
The researchers will take the following precautions to maintain the confidentiality of your data: All data will be deidentified so that responses remain anonymous in all subsequent analyses or written publications. Electronic data will be password-protected/encrypted. 
If your data collected as part of this research is used or distributed for future research studies, identifiers (e.g., any personal information that could potentially be used to identify you) will be removed.
Per DoDI 3216.02, study documents may be accessed by the Department of Defense for auditing purposes.
If you have questions regarding the study, contact the Principal Investigator: Dr. Thomas Carretta (thomas.carretta@us.af.mil). If you have questions regarding your rights as a research subject, contact the Air Force Research Laboratory Institutional Review Board (AFRL IRB) at afrl.ir.protocolmanagement@us.af.mil. An IRB, also called an ethics committee, is an independent committee that has reviewed this study to protect the rights and welfare of human research participants.
